learning_objective: 🎯 Measure the mathematical chance of events happening, from tossing coins and rolling dice to picking cards from a 52-card deck!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The probability of an event 'E' happening is calculated as: P(E) = (Number of outcomes favorable to E) / (Total number of possible outcomes).
Probability always lies between 0 and 1. (0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1). A probability of 0 means the event is 'Impossible'. A probability of 1 means it is a 'Sure Event'.
The probability of an event happening plus the probability of it NOT happening is exactly 1. Formula: P(E) + P(not E) = 1. (or P(E) + P(E̅) = 1).
A standard deck has 52 cards divided into 4 suits (Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs), 13 cards each. There are 12 'Face Cards' in total (Jacks, Queens, Kings).

fun_activity.title: 🪙 The Double Coin Toss
fun_activity.instructions: Take two coins and flip them together 10 times. Write down the outcomes (HH, HT, TH, TT). Because there are 4 possible outcomes, the theoretical probability of getting two heads (HH) is 1/4 (25%). Did your experiment match the math?

exam_tips: 📌 Remember that an Ace is NOT a face card. Only Jack, Queen, and King have faces printed on them.
📌 When two dice are thrown together, the total number of outcomes is 6 × 6 = 36. Always draw the 6x6 grid in rough work to avoid missing outcomes.
📌 The sum of the probabilities of all the elementary events of an experiment is always exactly 1.
quick_recap: ⭐ An event having only one outcome of the experiment is called an elementary event.
⭐ Red suits are Hearts and Diamonds; Black suits are Spades and Clubs.
⭐ The probability of getting a '7' when rolling a standard 6-sided die is 0 (Impossible event).
